{{Quote|I am Trinto Duaba, though, you may never tell. I sink into shadows. I ''am'' a shadow.|Trinto Duaba|<ref name="SS" />}}
The '''Stennes Shifters''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Near-Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Stennaros/Legends|Stennaros]]. They were biological offshoots of the [[Stennes]] and resembled their kin in appearance, with [[Color/Legends|ashen-gray]] skin riddled with dark veins and small knobs, a slight body, heavy-lidded [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and gaunt cheeks that gave them a [[Bone/Legends|skull]]-like visage. Yet the Shifters had several unique abilities that set them apart from their mainline cousins, all of which were rooted in an innate [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitivity]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Foremost was their ability to pass unseen using a form of [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathy]]. A Stennes Shifter could use this talent to disappear into a crowd. Shifters also were able to feed on the Force expended by beings around them. Such abilities earned the Stennes Shifters the alternate name of '''Force-eaters'''.

Environmental pressures shunted the Stennes Shifters along a different developmental path from their baseline cousins; their extra capacities to hide and sap Force energy helped the Shifters as both [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] and [[Diet/Legends|prey]] in their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld's]] ecosystem. However, such abilities also made the Shifters seem frightening and suspicious to both the mainline Stennes and to outsiders. Thus, the Shifters constantly found themselves persecuted, hunted, and&mdash;when discovered&mdash;[[Death/Legends|killed]]. As offworlders took to eradicating the Shifters&mdash;including the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in one particularly [[Blood/Legends|bloody]] [[Unidentified Stennes Shifter–Jedi conflict|conflict]] circa [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]&mdash;the planet became pocked with [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] craters in attacks that killed Stennes Shifters and standard Stennes alike. The Stennes turned on their Shifter kin, forcing them to flee their own homeworld or to use their natural powers to escape detection and assimilate into society. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the Shifter population fell; by the days of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], they were numbered at no more than several million, and the Shifters were regarded as little more than legend by many in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Coupled with their indistinguishable appearance from mainline Stennes, such anonymity allowed some Shifters to blend into [[Galactic community|galactic society]]. Those who capitalized on their powers of misperception found work in fringe occupations, such as thieves, [[Spy/Legends|spies]], or [[Information broker/Legends|informants]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|You 'pure' humans remark that we look sad, sullen, ghostly. But a rare few are Stennes Shifters. We are the privileged, for we can shade the eyes. We can shade the mind.|Trinto Duaba|<ref name="SS" />}}
[[File:Spooky_Shifter_SWAJ12.png|thumb|left|125px|Stennes Shifters had gaunt features.]]
The Stennes Shifters were a [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="SWC" /> of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] [[Near-Human]]s native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Stennaros/Legends|Stennaros]]. They were closely related to the [[Stennes]] species, from whom they evolved.<ref name="SS" /> Like standard Stennes, Shifters were generally quite thin,<ref name="SS" /> with a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body of two [[Limb/Legends|arms]], two legs, a torso, and a head in the same general proportions as a [[Human/Legends|Human]]. Their hands featured five digits apiece, each capped by a fingernail.<ref name="Hasbro" /> Shifters stood between 1.3 and 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="SS" />

The Shifter visage was composed of two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a [[Nose/Legends|nose]], a [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]], and rounded [[Ear/Legends|ears]] on the sides of the head. Members of the species had no noticeable lips,<ref name="Hasbro" /> and their [[Color/Legends|black]] eyes<ref name="CSWE I TD" /> were recessed into the [[Bone/Legends|skull]] and rimmed by dark circles. Coupled with their pale, gray skin, their features made Shifters appear to outsiders like morose [[Ghost (folklore)/Legends|ghosts]] with skull-like faces.<ref name="SS" /> In at least some Shifters,<ref name="SS" /> yellowish blotches and dark, purplish veins marbled<ref name="Hasbro" /> the rough skin.<ref name="CRC">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref>

Although their physiology gave no indication of special abilities, Stennes Shifters possessed a form of [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathy]] that allowed them to cloud the perceptions of others and thus allow the Shifter to go unnoticed. Those familiar with the ability often mistook it for [[Changeling/Legends|shape-shifting]], but it altered only the observer's perceptions, not the Shifter's physical form. The power only worked in situations when multiple entities were present; a Shifter could not pass unnoticed without a crowd in the area, and the ability was most potent in crowds of 100 beings or more. Members of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] species<ref name="SS" /> and artificial optic devices, such as [[Camera/Legends|cameras]] and [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]], could not be fooled by the Shifters' power.<ref name="SS" />

[[Scientist/Legends|Scientists]] speculated that the Stennes Shifter's mind-clouding was a manifestation of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], and, indeed, all Shifters were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]]. Rumors made them "Force vampires," able to sap others of the Force energy that flowed through them. Such stories had some basis in fact, as Shifters indeed could gain power from Force-users around them. However, the faculty only allowed a Shifter to absorb ''expended'' Force energy, that channeled within the vicinity of a Stennes Shifter. The Shifter then could absorb the exuded energy for his or her own use&mdash;but not tap into unused Force potential. Those conscious of a Shifter's attempt to absorb such Force power could willfully resist the Shifter's absorption. These abilities earned the Shifters an alternate name: Force-eaters.<ref name="SS" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Some find it offensive, some find it alluring, some find it frightening. It is merely a survival technique. To avoid predators. To aid in hunting.|Trinto Duaba|<ref name="SS" />}}
Within the confines of their home [[Stennaros system/Legends|star system]], Stennes Shifters exhibited the same affable nature and cultural advancement as baseline Stennes. However, they suffered from two layers of persecution. For one, non-Stennes distrusted the Shifters, fearful of their capabilities to pass unnoticed and to sap away the strength of others. Such prejudices were mostly unwarranted; while some Shifters did live as [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] and [[Death/Legends|killers]], such persecution forced many others to keep constant watch for aggressors. Secondly, even baseline Stennes turned against the Shifters in their species' history, attempting to eradicate the Shifters from the population of their mutual [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], Stennaros. Thus most Shifters lived inconspicuous lives, attempting to escape undue attention by laying low, pretending to be regular Stennes, and using their natural gifts of camouflage.<ref name="SS" /> Shifters could wear standard humanoid [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]], such as [[shirt]]s, trousers, [[Boot/Legends|boots]], and belts. Some members of the species received [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] implants. Shifters could wield standard weapons, such as [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]].<ref name="Hasbro" />

==History==
{{Quote|As civilization spread through the Stennes sector, we either became prized commodities, or hunted. That is the way with humans, near or otherwise. But we are not easy prey. How can you hunt what you cannot see? Or rather, how can you hunt what you cannot help but not see?|Trinto Duaba|<ref name="SS" />}}
The Stennes Shifters evolved on the planet of Stennaros, separating from the mainline Stennes during the ancient history of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Unlike their baseline counterparts, the Shifters evolved their capacity to alter the perceptions of others as a technique both to evade [[Diet/Legends|predators]] on their homeworld and to obtain prey of their own.<ref name="SS" />

As the [[Har Worlds|Stennes sector]] was colonized from afar and new settlers spread throughout it, prejudices against the Shifters spread. Outsiders took to hunting Shifters for sport or from fear. Stennaros itself became the target of purges to [[Speciecide|wipe out]] the Shifters, and violent campaigns left its surface pocked with craters from [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] strikes. In one incident, approximately 5,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Shifters faced the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in a [[Unidentified Stennes Shifter–Jedi conflict|conflict]], which convinced the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] that the Shifters were a dangerous threat. Prejudices against the Shifters ran so deep that mainline Stennes suffered as well. Eventually, the non-Shifter Stennes turned on their kin. The Stennes adopted [[Speciesism/Legends|xenophobic]] programs to detect Shifters in the general population and then eradicate them. Thousands of persecuted Shifters considered themselves to have lost a homeworld.<ref name="SS" />

By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Stennaros had fallen within the bounds of the [[Har Worlds]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]],<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}.</ref> but the Stennes Shifters nearly had been wiped out. Records of the species' early history were lost over the millennia so that, by the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the remaining data was difficult to understand. Imperial estimates suggested that as few as a thousand Shifters&mdash;and no more than several million&mdash;remained in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="SS" /> Nevertheless, Imperial interest in the Shifters remained; the [[Imperial Liaison Officer of Sentientology Studies]], [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Vontenn]],<ref name="GG4r">[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref> ordered the Human [[sentientologist]] [[Obo Rin]] to research the Stennes Shifters and add an entry on them to the scientist's work-in-progress, the ''[[Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy]]''.<ref name="SS" />

==Stennes Shifters in the galaxy==
[[File:Trinto-duaba.jpg|thumb|right||The Stennes Shifter Trinto Duaba patronized Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina.]]
Although some Stennes Shifters attempted to pass as baseline Stennes on their home planet, other Shifters took the attitude that they had no homeworld of which to speak. Instead, these Shifters immigrated to other worlds, where they used their natural talents in careers as [[Information broker/Legends|informants]], [[Spy/Legends|spies]], and thieves. Nevertheless, Shifters at large had to keep on their guard, since Humans and other species considered them untrustworthy at best, deadly at worst. While most non-Stennes dismissed the Shifters as legends with no basis in fact, those who encountered the so-called Force vampires reacted with occasional intrigue but, more often, terror.<ref name="SS" />

[[Trinto Duaba/Legends|Trinto Duaba]] was a Stennes Shifter active during the Galactic Civil War. He enjoyed disappearing into crowds and observing others&mdash;without himself being observed.<ref name="SWC" /> Duaba wore a hooded cloak to mask his features, and he sported cybernetic implants in his temples. He earned his living by identifying anyone wanted by the Galactic Empire<ref name="Hasbro" /> and then informing the [[Police officer/Legends|police]]<ref name="ISWOSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> or bringing the wanted person in himself.<ref name="Hasbro" /> Duaba was present at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]]'' on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] when the Human [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] hired the services of the Human [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] first mate, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> He patronized the cantina again later that year when the Empire declared a curfew on the planet.<ref name="SWHS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref><ref name="blog WW">{{SW|url=news/the-star-wars-holiday-special-cantina-we-may-not-thrive-friend-but-we-survive-friend|text=''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' Cantina: Who's Who|int=The Star Wars Holiday Special Cantina: Who's Who|nolive=1}}</ref> Duaba was forthright about his species with at least one individual: he talked at length with the [[Shi'ido]] [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Vandolae]] about the Stennes Shifters. The information later reached the Imperial sentientologist Obo Rin.<ref name="SS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You were actually our nightmare. Because when we made these things, there was this standard phrase: 'If anyone is looking at the [background], we're really screwed.'&nbsp;|Makeup artist [[Nick Maley]] on the fan scrutiny that has identified masks such as the Terminal Man and his mustachioed counterpart|<ref name="MBB">{{SW|url=news/meet-braconnor-bakiska|text=Meet Braconnor Bakiska}}</ref>}}
[[File:BrandonConnorsTomSpina-CelebrationVI.jpg|thumb|left|Celebration VI attendee Brandon Connors and effects artist Tom Spina show off a replica of the second Stennes mask used in ''A New Hope''.]]
Special effects artist [[Rick Baker]] designed what would eventually become the Stennes Shifters as a Halloween mask. With its monstrous appearance and electrical terminals on its temples, Baker intended for the mask to represent Frankenstein's monster.<ref name="MBB" /> When director [[George Lucas]] hired Baker to create creatures for use during additional photography for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] in Los Angeles, he and his team created several new [[Alien/Legends|alien]] masks to populate closeup shots for the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] sequence of the film. Baker added his Halloween mask in an effort to fill out the roster. The character went by the name "Terminal Man" during the film's production, both due to the terminally ill look and the electric terminals on his head. Other nicknames included "Veiny" and "Future Man."<ref name="CRC" /> One of the other Los Angeles&ndash;based special effects artists made a copy of the Terminal Man mask, and added a mustache and hair for use as another cantina extra.<ref name="MBB" /> The characters' scenes were shot on [[January 24]] and [[January 25|25]], [[1977]].<ref name="MOSW">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> One of these two masks was reused for the cantina scene in the [[1978]] telefilm ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.<ref name="Starlog">"Star Wars Invades TV", [[Wikipedia:Starlog|''Starlog'']] 19, February 1979</ref>

In [[1995]], the game company [[Decipher]], provided the first official name for the hairless Terminal Man on a card for their [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]]. The company dubbed him Trinto Duaba and made him a Stennes Shifter.<ref name="TD CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Trinto Duaba}}</ref> Decipher's use of the word ''Stennes'' was a misspelling, but it has since been accepted into [[canon]].<ref name="MBB" /> The card's lore was the first indication of the Shifters' Force-absorption ability.<ref name="CRC" /> Author [[Pablo Hidalgo]] expanded on Decipher's work to provide the first detailed background information on Stennes Shifters in his article "[[Shape-shifters]]," which was published in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 12|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 12]] in [[1997]]. The article provides rules to use Shifters in [[West End Games]]' [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars'' roleplaying game]]; while they are average in most respects, they can use game mechanics to absorb Force points expended by those around them.<ref name="SS" /> Finally, the toy company [[Hasbro]] released an action figure of Trinto Duaba in [[2008]], pairing him with [[Dice Ibegon/Legends|Dice Ibegon]], another cantina character from ''A New Hope''. Hasbro's toy was the first source to show a Shifter's full body.<ref name="Hasbro" />

The mustachioed version of Terminal Man went unnamed in official ''Star Wars'' lore for years until [[Tom Spina]], an artist with extensive experience repairing and duplicating props used in the ''Star Wars'' films, made a replica of the mask as a prize for an attendee of [[2012]]'s [[Celebration VI]] fan convention. In a nod to the winner, [[Brandon Connors]], the character was dubbed [[Braconnor Bakiska/Legends|Braconnor Bakiska]].<ref name="MBB" /> Because Bakiska and the ''Holiday Special'' character only appear on screen briefly,<ref name="ANH" /><ref name="SWHS" /> the films do not make clear whether they are standard Stennes or Stennes Shifters.<ref name="SS" /> However, the article "[[The Star Wars Holiday Special Cantina: Who's Who|The ''Star Wars Holiday Special'' Cantina: Who's Who]]," by [[Tim Veekhoven]] and [[Kevin Beentjes]], identifies the ''Holiday Special'' character as Duaba.<ref name="blog WW" />
